newsitem.title: USA: GM building ignition systems plant in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: GM building ignition systems plant in Mexico.

text.p: General Motors Corp.'s Delphi Energy & Engine Management Systems division said it has begun construction of a new automotive ignition components plant in Torreon, Mexico.

The plant, scheduled to begin operations in fall 1997, will produce a new-generation ignition system that places the ignition coil near the spark plug. The Delphi unit's Anderson, Indiana, plant also will begin producing the coil-near-plug systems in 1998, GM spokesman Dan Dolan said.
The system, which will be used in many future GM cars and trucks, is expected to deliver a more powerful spark to engines, improving horsepower, fuel economy and emissions performance.
Dolan declined to reveal GM's investment in the Torreon facility.
The Torreon plant will employ about 500 people when it reaches full production, Dolan said. The new product is not expected to add jobs at the Anderson plant, but is expected to preserve jobs.
"They'll evolve from what they're making now into this type of component," Dolan said.
Delphi Energy & Engine Management also currently produces other ignition systems and compents in Piracicaba, Brazil; Taegu, South Korea; Chihuahua, Mexico; and Seixal, Portugal.
